tasks.spec:
YOUR LANE: TEST-COVERAGE GAP. tests/test_id_pinned_search.py exists, covers id-pinned search, and passes. Production nevertheless returns an empty result for exactly that case. Explain that contradiction. Read the test file closely and determine what it actually asserts versus what the live request path actually does: what the tests construct by hand rather than exercise, which layer they enter at, whether they call the real handler or a helper beneath it, and what they stub or fake. Then state the single missing test that would have caught this, precisely enough that someone could write it. Your value is explaining why the safety net had a hole.

BOUNDARY, read this before anything else. You are READ-ONLY with respect to the source under review. Everything you need is staged in ./sources/ in your current task directory. NEVER modify, delete, or rewrite any file under ./sources/. NEVER run git. NEVER commit. NEVER call a network endpoint or external API — the live system is not reachable from here and you must not try. NEVER load skills, call MCP tools or Apps, or capture notes to any external memory or knowledge base. The ONLY file you create is ./findings.json in your current task directory.

THE PROBLEM. A booking gateway exposes POST /patient-search. Queried by last name it returns 199 patients. Queried by patient_id it returns an empty result — including for an id that appears inside that very name-search result set. The patient provably exists. Read ./sources/EVIDENCE.md FIRST; it contains every live measurement, the exact request bodies, the responses, and a lead that may well be wrong.

WHAT IS STAGED IN ./sources/:
- EVIDENCE.md — the live measurements. Read first.
- container/bland_gateway.py — the HTTP handler. This is the main artifact.
- container/capability_registry.py, container/feed_task.py, container/session_warm.py — supporting modules.
- tests/test_id_pinned_search.py — tests that specifically cover id-pinned search and currently pass.
- tests/test_bland_gateway.py, tests/test_recall_context.py, tests/test_webhook_capabilities.py — further tests.
- DESIGN.md, Dockerfile.

SCOPE WARNING. bland_gateway.py is shared code. The same container image serves a second live client's booking lane. Any fix you imply must state whether it changes behavior for callers other than the id-pinned recall path.

WRITE ./findings.json AS A SINGLE JSON OBJECT WITH EXACTLY THESE KEYS:
  schema_version  string, exactly "gw-patient-search-diagnosis.v1"
  lane            string naming your lane
  root_cause      object {statement, mechanism, confidence}. statement is at least 60 characters saying what is actually wrong. mechanism is at least 60 characters tracing HOW a patient_id request becomes an empty result, naming the functions and branches involved. confidence is exactly one of high, medium, low.
  evidence        array of objects {quote, file, why}. quote must be copied character-for-character from a staged file and be at least 25 characters. file names which staged file it came from. why is at least 30 characters. An automated validator checks every quote against the staged files; a quote that does not appear verbatim fails the task. At least three must ground.
  disproof        string, at least 40 characters, naming a concrete observation that would REFUTE your root cause. If you cannot say what would prove you wrong, you have not diagnosed anything.
  shared_impact   string, at least 40 characters, on whether the implied fix changes behavior for the other client.
  recommended_fix string describing the narrowest change that would fix it. Describe it; do NOT implement it.

HARD RULES. Do not propose a fix you cannot ground in the staged code. Do not claim high confidence on a mechanism you did not verify. If the evidence points somewhere other than the lead in EVIDENCE.md, say so plainly; that lead is a hypothesis, not a conclusion. Output valid JSON only in ./findings.json, no prose, no code fences.
tasks.verified: the lane produced a falsifiable root cause with at least three quotes that appear verbatim in the staged gateway source, a stated disproof, and an assessment of whether its fix would affect the other client
